newsitem.title: UK: UK money market shrugs off 2.05 bln shortage.
newsitem.headline: UK money market shrugs off 2.05 bln shortage.

text.p: The UK money market dealt smoothly with an unexpectedly large 2.05 billion stg liquidity shortage on Friday, with cash rates softening slightly compared with the previous fortnight.
* The Bank of England provided assistance totalling 2.056 billion stg.
* Overnight cash was quoted at 5 7/8 3/4 in late trade. Dealers say around a billion stg worth of repos are still around which should smooth things over next week.
* On the gilt repo market, traders say 8.0 percent gilts due 2003 remained the main special, trading at 4.5 percent overnight and 4.75 percent for the week.
* The 7.0 percent gilt due 2001 was trading at 25 basis points under general collateral rates for one month, with the 6.0 percent gilt due 1999 around the same level.
* Dealers said the major movement of the day was a curve steepening. The three month rate has gone to 5.85 percent bid from 5.75 percent.
* Overnight general collateral eased around 10 basis points from yesterday, to be quoted at 4.75 percent in late trade, having spiked to 6.0 percent at one point.

* Former discount houses Gerrard & National and King & Shaxson Holdings announced they are to join forces creating a broking and specialist banking group with 10 billion pounds of funds under management.
